readout_other: genioglossus EMG; pulse oximetry; 33 MHz needle-transducer M-mode tongue displacement; H&E and HIF-1alpha IHC; tissue temperature
direction_notes: LIPUS of the hypoglossal nerve increased phasic and tonic genioglossus EMG with intensity, increased tongue displacement and oxygen saturation; effects vanished after nerve transection.
safety_notes: H&E and HIF-1alpha staining showed no tissue damage; temperature during stimulation rose from 28.27 C baseline to 30.83 C at 5 min.

exposures.label: LIPUS to hypoglossal nerve (US1 to US3)

timing.protocol_description: Tone burst of 500 us, 50% duty cycle, PRF 1 kHz, applied at Ispta 354, 510 and 667 mW/cm2 (US1-US3) for 15-60 s until a response was observed, within non-stimulation, stimulation and post-stimulation phases.

source_quotes.n_subjects: A total of 18 genetically unmodified C57BL/6 mice aged 4–12 weeks were subjected to the previously described stimulation protocol.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: A 1-MHz ultrasound transducer was applied to the cervical region of anesthetized mice to deliver acoustic stimulation.
source_quotes.exposures[0].unspecified_domain.ispta_w_: LIPUS stimulation was applied to HN at spatial peak temporal average intensities of 354 mW/cm<sup>2</sup> (US1), 510 $\mathrm { m W } / \mathrm { c m } ^ { 2 }$ (US2), and 667 mW/cm<sup>2</sup> (US3) for 15–60 s until a response was observed.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: An excitation signal was identified as a tone burst with a duration of 500 $\mu \mathrm { s } ,$ a duty cycle of 50%, and a pulse repetition frequency of 1 kHz.

source_quotes.exposures[0].device.model: Ultrasound excitation signals were generated using a function generator (AFG 3022B; Tektronix, Irving, TX, USA) connected through a radiofrequency power amplifier (25A250A; Amplifier Research, Souderton, PA, USA) to a 1-MHz single-element transducer (A314S, focal length = 80 mm, focus zone = 10 mm; Olympus, Waltham, MA, USA) for stimulation.
